GlanceRead.description: Home's budget at a glance for the month.

IncomePartIn.title: IncomePartIn

MergeResult.description: What merging one account into another did (or, for a dry run, would do).
MergeResult.title: MergeResult

OpeningBalanceCreate.description:
What a person already owed before finode: they owe you (`receivable`) or you owe them (`payable`). It touches none
of your accounts or budgets.
OpeningBalanceCreate.title: OpeningBalanceCreate

OpeningBalanceUpdate.description:
Changes to an opening balance: only what is sent changes. Once part of it has been paid back, the amount cannot go
below that and who owes whom cannot change. `description` null clears the note.
OpeningBalanceUpdate.title: OpeningBalanceUpdate

ParticipantIn.description:
Who shares the expense: you (`is_self`) or a contact. `value` is what the split method needs: nothing for an
equal split, the weight for `shares`, the percentage for `percentage` or the amount for `exact`.

PayeeSuggestions.title: PayeeSuggestions

PaymentIn.description: What you paid, from which of your accounts.

Money that came in, part of it not yours. Your income is the total less `theirs`; `deposits` and `received_by`

StepRead.description: A first step for a new person; the app knows where each `key` leads.

TagRead.description: A tag: how many entries carry it and the day of the latest.

TodoCard.description: A card's (or loan's) bill that is due within a few days or overdue, and still not paid.

TransactionPreview.description: What a dry run says would happen: the entry as it would be saved (nothing was saved).

TransferCreate.description: Money sent to a contact (a loan, an advance, a gift) or received from one (a borrowing, an advance, a gift).

get.description: Accounts with their balances as of a day (today by default: later entries do not count yet).

schema.title: Response Get Accounts Api Accounts  Get

post.description: Create an account under Assets, Liabilities or Equity (Expenses and Income hold categories: see /categories); `balance` sets an opening balance on an asset or liability.

get.description:
Accounts that were closed: the outermost of each closed branch, newest first. Reopen one with
POST /accounts/{account_id}/reopen.

schema.title: Response Closed Accounts Api Accounts Closed Get

post.description: Make a group, a shelf for accounts: under Assets (money you own) or Liabilities (money you owe). `new_accounts_in_budget` is what an account made in it starts as. A group has no balance and can be empty.

delete.description: Delete an account for good; refused when it has entries, sub-accounts or a recurring rule (close it instead).

get.description: The account with its balance as of a day (today by default: later entries do not count yet).

patch.description: Change an account: name, note, place (`parent_id`) or budget flag.

get.description:
A card's or loan's bill, worked out from its statement day and due day: what was owed when the latest statement
closed, less the payments and refunds since, when it is due, and what was spent since. Nothing is stored. 400 while
the account has no days.

Set a statement's balance against the books on the same day (today by default): the books' balance, the
difference and the entries of the last `days` days, with those exactly as large as the difference. Nothing is
changed. A card's or loan's balance is what is owed, as the app shows it.

post.description:
Close an account (and everything inside it): its history stays, nothing more can be posted to it.
Refused while it holds a balance or a recurring transaction still uses it.

Make this account part of another (`into`): its entries, recurring rules and shared bills become the
other's and it is deleted, all or nothing. Both must be plain accounts of the same top-level account
(this one without sub-accounts, the other open and able to take entries). Refused when an entry or rule has both on
opposite sides, or only one is part of the budget. With `dry_run=true` nothing changes and the answer says what
would move.

get.description:
The account's entries, oldest first, each with what it changed and the running balance. `own_only` leaves out
what was posted to its sub-accounts.

schema.title: Response Account Register Api Accounts  Account Id  Register Get

post.description: Reopen a closed account with everything inside it, and the groups above it.

get.description: The MCP address, your tokens and the apps you connected (revoked ones left out).

post.description: Take the app's access back, and ask Supabase to stop issuing it tokens.
A new token; its secret is in this answer only (just a hash is kept).
Email a reset link. The same answer whether or not the address has an account.

get.description: What the sign-in screens offer here: sign-up (invite only), forgotten password, the test notice.

post.description: Set a new password from the emailed link and sign in. A spent or expired link answers `code: link-invalid`.

get.description: Who is signed in, and today's date as finode counts it.

post.description: Invite-only: 404 unless sign-up is set up on this server.

get.description: A complete backup: settings, accounts, transactions, recurring rules and the budget.
The month's budget (the current month by default): what is left to assign and each category's figures.

post.description: Make an account part of the budget (its money and its spending count from now on).

put.description: Set how much of the month a spending category gets; 0 removes it.

get.description:
What is coming up after today, to the end of this month (or to `through`, at most a year ahead): entries dated
ahead and what recurring rules will record, those that touch an account of the budget, soonest first.

post.description: Assign a month what each category got the month before, where nothing is assigned yet (nothing is overwritten).

put.description: Set a group's budget for a month: at least what its subcategories add up to; the rest is the group's own money.

post.description: Move assigned money from one category to another (at most what is available); Ready to assign does not change.

get.description:
Your categories (what money was for): spending ones are what the budget plans against, earning ones label
income. A group has no parent; a category inside it names it as `parent_id`.

schema.title: Response List Categories Api Categories  Get

post.description:
Make a category, or a group (leave out `parent_id`) to put categories in. Two levels at most; names are unique
inside a group, capitals aside.

patch.description: Rename a category, change its note or move it into another group (`parent_id`; null takes it out of its group).

post.description: Close a category (and what is inside a group): its history stays, nothing more can be labelled with it.

Remove an unused category for good. One with history (entries, labelled lines, sub-categories or a recurring
rule) is closed instead, and the answer says which happened.

Fold this category into another (`into`, a category id): its entries, labelled lines, planned amounts and
recurring rules become the other's, and this one goes. Same rules as merging accounts; `dry_run=true` only tells
what would move.

get.description:
The entries that have a line labelled with the category (and with the categories in it, unless `own_only`),
oldest first, each with what it changed and the running total.

schema.title: Response Category Register Api Categories  Category Id  Register Get

get.description:
Your contacts, by name or (`sort=balance`) by how much is outstanding, the biggest first. Each carries the two
ledger accounts behind it ("Due from": they owe you, "Due to": you owe them), what each holds, and the day of the
latest thing done with them. `q` looks in name, email, phone and notes; `owing` keeps those who owe you
(`receivable`) or whom you owe (`payable`).

schema.title: Response List Contacts Api Contacts  Get

post.description: Add a contact; its two accounts are made with it. Names are unique, capitals aside, and at most 30 characters.

delete.description:
Remove a contact no money ever moved with. One with entries is archived instead (refused while anything is
owed), and the answer says which happened.

patch.description: Change a contact's name (its two accounts are renamed with it) or details; null clears email, phone or notes.

get.description:
Everything done with the contact (loans, borrowings, advances, gifts, shared expenses, settlements), newest
first, with the total count for paging.

post.description: Hide a contact from new entries; its history stays. Refused while anything is owed either way.

get.description:
What the contact owes you and what you owe them, one row per amount, oldest first, each with how much of it
has been settled and how much is left. `open_only` leaves out the settled ones.

schema.title: Response Contact Obligations Api Contacts  Contact Id  Obligations Get

post.description:
What the contact already owed you (`receivable`) or you owed them (`payable`) before you started with finode. It
is recorded against the Opening Balances account, so none of your accounts or budgets move, and it can be settled
like any other amount. Undo it with `DELETE /transfers/{transaction_id}`.

post.description:
Settle up: `received` is the contact paying back what they owe you, `sent` you paying back what you owe them.
`allocation_method` `fifo` clears the oldest amounts first, `manual` takes `allocations`. Nothing is cleared beyond
what is owed: more than that needs `excess_as` to say what the rest is. Send an `Idempotency-Key` header to make a
retry safe.

What a settlement would clear (which obligations, how much of each, what is left over and what is still owed),
saving nothing.

get.description:
What the books say about the contact (receivable, payable, net), what you lent and borrowed, the expenses you
shared and the settlements, how many obligations are open and the latest activity.
A contact's transfers, newest first.

schema.title: Response List Transfers Api Contacts  Contact Id  Transfers Get

post.description:
Money sent to a contact (`loan`, `advance`, `gift`) or received from one (`borrowing`, `advance`, `gift`). A
loan or advance leaves a receivable, a borrowing or received advance a payable, a gift nothing owed. Send an
`Idempotency-Key` header to make a retry safe.

get.description: What the data page offers: import and restore need empty books; the word Erase and Delete ask you to type.

post.description: Delete my account: everything, then the sign-in itself (needs Supabase's admin key on the server).
Erase my books: every entry, account, category, person, rule and budget; the profile and sign-in stay.

get.description: The app asking to connect (Supabase sends you to the app's consent screen with this id).

post.description: Allow (with an access level) or deny. The app recorded is whatever Supabase says this request is for.

get.description: The currencies you can choose for your books (changing it relabels, never converts).

schema.title: Response Currencies Api Profile Currencies Get

get.description: Every recurring rule (due occurrences are recorded first).

schema.title: Response List Recurring Api Recurring  Get

post.description: Create a rule: a simple one (from/to/amount) or a split (`postings`), on a schedule.

delete.description: Delete a rule; the transactions it recorded are kept.

get.description: One recurring rule.

put.description: Replace a rule's details; it continues after the last recorded or skipped day.

post.description: Stop recording a rule until it is resumed. What it already recorded is kept.
Start a paused rule again. What fell due while it was paused is skipped, not recorded late.
Leave the next occurrence out (nothing is recorded for it); the rule carries on with the one after.

get.description:
Where the money went (or came from) in a period, `depth` levels down: what it was for, as the Budget counts it
(paying into a loan is spending in its category).
Net worth now, plus income and expenses for a period (the current month so far by default).
Every account's debits and credits, plus a check that the books are sound.

post.description: Restore a backup into an empty ledger, all or nothing (`dry_run` shows what would happen).

delete.description:
Undo a settlement for good: what it cleared is owed again. Refused (409) once what its excess left owed has been
settled in turn.

get.description: Your shared expenses, newest first.

schema.title: Response List Shared Expenses Api Shared Expenses  Get

post.description:
Save an expense split with contacts as a draft, or with `confirm=true` record it at once. The shares are worked
out by `split_method` (`equal`, `exact` amounts, `percentage`, `shares` weights); `payments` are what you paid from
your accounts and `contributions` what contacts paid. Only a bill fully paid for can be confirmed.

parameters.description: Send the same key again after a timeout and the first result comes back instead of a second entry.
parameters.name: idempotency-key

schema.description: Send the same key again after a timeout and the first result comes back instead of a second entry.
schema.title: Idempotency-Key

post.description:
What an expense would do (each person's share, who owes whom, the ledger lines, and how much of the bill is
still unpaid for) with nothing saved. The same checks as saving, except that a bill not yet fully paid for is fine.

patch.description:
Change a draft (only what is sent changes; a list is replaced whole). A confirmed expense is cancelled and
entered again instead (409).

post.description:
Remove a draft, or reverse a confirmed expense for good: its entry and what it left owed go too. Refused (409)
once anything was settled against it.

Record the expense: one ledger entry (your share spent, your payments out) and what each contact owes or is owed.
Confirming twice is a 409; send an `Idempotency-Key` so a retry returns the first result.

parameters.name: idempotency-key

schema.description: Send the same key again after a timeout and the first result comes back instead of a second entry.
schema.title: Idempotency-Key

post.description:
Record money that came in, part of it not yours. `theirs` are the parts that belong to contacts (you owe them),
`received_by` money a contact received for you (they owe you), `deposits` what landed in your accounts. Your own part
is the total less `theirs`; deposits and `received_by` must add up to the total.

parameters.description: Send the same key again after a timeout and the first result comes back instead of a second entry.
parameters.name: idempotency-key

schema.description: Send the same key again after a timeout and the first result comes back instead of a second entry.
schema.title: Idempotency-Key

post.description:
What income shared with people would do (your own part, what you hold for others, who received it for you) with
nothing saved. The same checks as saving.

put.description:
Record it again with new parts: the entry keeps its id. Refused (409) once anything was paid back against it. An
ordinary income entry can be turned into shared income the same way.

post.description:
Reverse shared income for good: its entry and what it left owed go too. Refused (409) once anything was settled
against it.

get.description: Your tags, the most used first, each with how many entries carry it and the day of the latest.

schema.title: Response List Tags Api Tags  Get

delete.description: Take a tag off every entry and remove it. The entries stay as they are.

patch.description: Rename a tag; when the new name is another of your tags the two become one (a merge).

get.description: What needs a decision now: payments no category took, accounts left out of the budget, failing recurring rules.

Newest first. `text` matches the payee, the note or the name of an account used; `kind` is told by the accounts
used (spending, income or a transfer); `category_id` is a category the entry must also touch;
`payee` is exact, capitals aside; `source` and `external_id` find the entry a source's reference stands for; `tag` finds
entries whose note has that #hashtag.

schema.title: Response Get Transactions Api Transactions  Get

post.description:
Record a transaction: postings whose debits equal their credits (at least two), a date (today by default), payee, note and optional `related_id`.
`source`, `external_id` and `source_url` say where it came from (a bank, a mail); a source's reference is used once,
so sending the same one again with the same date and rows answers 200 with the entry already recorded, and
nothing is created. The same reference with a different date or rows is a 400.
With `dry_run=true` every check runs but nothing is saved: the answer (200) is the entry as it would be saved.

schema.title: Response Create Transaction Api Transactions  Post

post.description:
Record up to 50 transactions as one: all are saved or none. An entry whose `source` and `external_id` are already
recorded with the same date and rows is skipped (status `already_recorded`), so a batch can be sent again safely.
Any problem refuses the whole batch (400) naming the entries at fault. With `dry_run=true` nothing is saved and the
answer (200) shows what would be.

get.description:
How payees are usually booked, most used first: the accounts of the newest entry with one account on each side
(so a repeat can be filled in), and the other routes seen. `payee` narrows to those that match what is typed.

schema.title: Response Payee Defaults Api Transactions Payee Defaults Get

get.description:
The Add screen's chips: names of people you pay that match what is typed (most paid first), or after an "@"
your people; `only=people` offers people only. Names only, never accounts.
Who you have paid or been paid by, most used first (the opening-balance entries are left out).

schema.title: Response Payees Api Transactions Payees Get

delete.description:
Delete a transaction for good.
With `dry_run=true` nothing is deleted: the answer (200) is the entry that would go.

get.description: One transaction with its postings.

patch.description:
Change a transaction; only the fields sent change (`related_id: null` removes the link; `source`, `external_id` and `source_url` can be set or, with null, cleared).
With `dry_run=true` every check runs but nothing is saved: the answer is the entry as it would read afterwards.

schema.title: Response Update Transaction Api Transactions  Transaction Id  Patch

get.description: The entries that are related to this one (refunds, reversals), oldest first.

schema.title: Response Related Transactions Api Transactions  Transaction Id  Related Get

delete.description:
Undo a transfer for good: its entry, what it left owed and its activity go. Refused (409) once anything was
settled against what it left owed; reverse that settlement first.

patch.description:
Change an opening balance (`amount`, `date`, `description`, `direction`); only what is sent changes. Once part of
it was paid back, the amount can't go below that (400) and who owes whom can't change (409). Other transfers are
reversed and recorded again.

get.description:
Home for a month (`YYYY-MM`, never ahead): the budget at a glance, the month's first entries (a day is never cut;
the rest come from `/views/transactions`), and a new person's first steps while some are left.
The choices behind the Transactions screen's Filter sheet: accounts, categories (with their parent) and payees.

A page of one month's entries for the Transactions screen, newest first up to today (a day is never split between
pages: the next page starts at `offset + len(rows)`). With an account, category, merchant or tag filter, `summary`
adds up everything that matches; on the first page of the current month, `upcoming` lists what is dated ahead.
One entry as its details sheet shows it.
